Job Description

In short: We're looking for a Software Engineer to join our foundation team with a focus on mobile. You don't need to have years of experience in platform engineering But, you do need to have shipped real production software, to care about how things are built, and to already be working with agentic coding tools every day.

We're building the #1 AI learning companion for 1 billion students. A future where every student on the planet can access, enjoy & benefit from the highest quality education. Since founding Knowunity straight out of high school in 2020, we've been committed to revolutionising how students learn.

Millions of students already use our AI learning companion weekly. We just raised €27m - Europe’s largest education round in the past three years. The AI learning market is at an inflection point, finally enabling true personalisation at scale, and we're determined to build the first AI learning unicorn in this space.

You will join an elite team of +60 hands-on builders serving 1 billion students worldwide. If we execute on our product vision, you will have built something generational that transforms education globally. This is your chance to build a generational company that shapes how an entire generation learns.

 


What makes this different

You build at the frontier of AI engineering. We’re building the foundation for agents to build fast and with high quality on our code base. This includes custom MCP servers, our background agent platform, and end-to-end agentic loops. This is an open engineering problem, not a solved one, and you'll be shaping our answer to it.

Your work multiplies across 25+ engineers. A design system component you build gets used in a hundred screens. A CI pipeline you cut from 15 minutes to 2 gives the whole org back a day a week. Foundation is the highest-leverage place in our engineering org, and the leverage is measurable.

Millions of students use what you ship. Foundation isn't a team that only builds for other engineers. You'll also build features that land in front of millions of users.

Real ownership, early. We're a small team with a large surface. You'll own meaningful pieces of the app and the toolchain from your first months.

Craft is taken seriously. We care how the app feels: how a sheet animates, how a list scrolls under load, how a component behaves at the edges. If you've ever been quietly annoyed by four pixels, you'll fit in here.

Find out more here!: This AI studying app with 25M+ downloads is built with Flutter

 


What you'll work on

Mobile foundation. The core of our Flutter app: shared components, the design system, state management, performance, and the tooling around it. You'll extend it, keep it healthy, and make it obvious for product teams to use correctly.

Agentic and AI infrastructure. MCP servers, our background agent platform, evals and feedback loops, and the integration of agentic tooling into our day-to-day workflow. A research background isn't required; a serious interest in agents as an engineering discipline is.

Developer experience. CI/CD, release tooling, and the feedback loop between writing code and seeing it live. Much of this work starts by noticing the same friction three times and deciding to remove it.

Product features. Shipping user-facing work alongside platform work, both to move the product and to stay honest about what it's actually like to build on our foundation.

Reliability and maintenance. Keeping what exists dependable, so 25+ engineers can build on it without thinking about it.



You will grow at Knowunity by

  • Learning architecture by doing it. You'll make real design decisions on the app's core, with review and mentorship from engineers who have architected mobile apps at scale. You'll see those decisions tested by 25 engineers and millions of users within weeks.

  • Becoming genuinely strong at agentic engineering. Almost nobody is an expert here yet. You'll be building the practice for a whole engineering org while the field is still being written.

  • Widening past mobile. Foundation's scope covers Go services, infrastructure, and delivery. You'll be expected to have opinions beyond the app, and you'll have the room to develop them.

  • Working close to the whole org. Platform work means talking to every team. You'll get an unusually complete picture of how a product organisation actually functions, faster than you would inside a single product team.

  • Operating at real scale. Millions of users, 26 countries, and a codebase where "it works on my machine" isn't the finish line.



What we're looking for

Must haves

  • A few years of production experience building mobile (we use Flutter and Dart) or web applications.

  • Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, or similar) and opinions on where they work well, where they don't, and how to work around it.

  • An eye for design. You notice when spacing is inconsistent, when an animation feels wrong, when a component is close but not right.

  • Clear communication in English and a genuine preference for improving systems that slow other people down, whether or not your name ends up on a shipped feature.

Nice to haves

  • Built mobile apps with Flutter

  • Worked with Golang (or similar backend language)

  • Anything you've built with agents, MCP, or evals.

Ideals is a global B2B SaaS product company recognized as the most highly rated and customer-centric brand in the secure business collaboration market. Ideals Virtual Data Room (VDR): Secure document sharing and collaboration for due diligence, fundraising, corporate reporting, licensing, clinical trials, and other complex transactions.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

We're hiring Value Engineering Interns (6-month period) and Working Students (15-20h per week, preferable with full-time internship in the first 2 months) to join our team. You'll work closely with our Value Engineering Manager and with our Account Executives on live enterprise deals and lifting our operations to the next level.

Depending on where the business's priorities sit at any given time, your day-to-day will flex between two areas of our Value Engineering work:

  • Customer-Facing Value Engineering: supporting our account teams (Account Executive, Value Engineer) directly on deals

  • Value Engineering & Applied AI: building the models, tools, and content that make our own pre-sales function faster and more consistent

What You’ll Own

On customer-facing work

  • Help uncover where value is trapped in P2P, AP, S2P, and O2C/AR processes, and the real problem underneath the stated one.

  • Turn customer data into business cases: FTE capacity, cycle time, controls, compliance risk, and TCO.

  • Help prepare and run tailored demos, workshops, and executive presentations for CFO, CIO, and Shared Services audiences.

  • Support Proof of Value (PoV) engagements, from data preparation and analysis to the results readout.

  • Research and sharpen our positioning against point tools (OCR, IDP, workflow, RPA, process mining).

On value engineering and applied AI work

  • Build a scalable deep-dive knowledge platform to facilitate knowledge exchange with available AI tools (LLMs, AI assistants, workflow automation) to speed up research, analysis, and deliverable creation

  • Build and improve ROI models, business case templates, and value driver frameworks.

  • Keep demo data and narrative up to date and scalable

What we're looking for

  • Currently enrolled in a Master's program in business, finance, information systems, industrial engineering, economics, or a related field.

  • Interest in finance and procurement processes such as AP, invoice processing, P2P, and O2C.

  • Strong analytical skills and comfort turning messy data into a clear, quantified story, including in Excel or Google Sheets.

  • Hands-on experience with AI tools (LLMs, AI assistants, or workflow automation), or confidence that you'll pick them up fast.

  • Clear communication: you can make a complex topic simple, in writing and live.

  • Curiosity and the confidence to respectfully question assumptions.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity and fast feedback cycles.

  • Fluent English, German is a plus.

  • Bonus: prior experience in consulting, presales, finance, procurement, or SaaS; exposure to ERP or business-process environments (SAP S/4HANA, ECC, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, NetSuite); experience with process mining tools; other European languages.

What you'll get

  • Live work, not a training exercise. Everything you touch supports real deals with real enterprise customers.

  • Work at the frontier. Use and apply the latest AI tooling in ERP automation.

  • A clear, fast path to a permanent role. For the right candidates.

data.description:
Deine Mission

Das Produkt steht. Jetzt entscheidet sich, wie wir darüber sprechen.

Das ist kein Callcenter-Job. Keine Kaltakquise, keine gekaufte Liste, keine Quote pro Stunde.
Du kontaktierst Betriebe, die uns bereits kennen. Installationspartner, mit denen wir seit Monaten oder Jahren arbeiten. Sie wissen, wer Bees & Bears ist — sie wissen nur noch nicht, was wir gerade Neues für sie gebaut haben.

Warum es diese Stelle gibt: Wir bringen ein neues Produkt an den Start, das unseren Partnerbetrieben einen konkreten Engpass löst. Technisch ist es fertig. Was jetzt zählt, ist die Einführung — und die passiert nicht über eine Mail. Sie passiert in Gesprächen.

Deine Aufgabe: Diese Gespräche führen. Du bekommst eine Einarbeitung und einen Gesprächsleitfaden. Nach acht Wochen sollte auch dieser Leitfaden noch besser sein, weil du hundert Gespräche geführt hast. Wer nur die Liste abarbeiten will, ist hier falsch. Wer wartet, bis jemand den nächsten Schritt vorgibt, auch.

Wohin die Rolle wächst: Sie startet fokussiert: ein Produkt, ein definierter Partnerkreis, ein Gespräch nach dem anderen. Sie ist aber nicht als Telefonjob angelegt, sondern als Einstieg ins Partner Management — eigene Partner, Ende zu Ende, von Erstkontakt bis laufender Betreuung. Wie schnell das geht, hängt an dir, nicht an einem Kalender.

Konkret:

  • ANRUFEN, NICHT ABTELEFONIEREN: Du stellst das neue Produkt bei Bestandspartnern vor. Nicht Skript vom Blatt, sondern ein Gespräch, das beim Gegenüber ankommt.
  • DEN PITCH WEITERENTWICKELN: Du merkst, welcher Einstieg funktioniert und welcher Einwand immer wieder kommt. Du behältst das nicht für dich, du änderst den Leitfaden.
  • ZUHÖREN UND ZURÜCKSPIELEN: Was Partner am Telefon sagen, ist die ehrlichste Rückmeldung, die wir zum Produkt bekommen. Du bist die direkteste Leitung dorthin und nutzt sie.
  • BEZIEHUNG STATT KONTAKTLISTE: Du übernimmst einen festen Kreis von Partnern. Nach drei Monaten kennen die deinen Namen, nicht unsere Rufnummer.
  • SAUBER NACHHALTEN: Was besprochen wurde, landet nachvollziehbar in Hubspot, damit das Team damit weiterarbeiten kann.


Dein Talent

  • SUSTAINABILITY: Du interessierst dich sehr für Klimaschutz und Nachhaltigkeit und willst mehr darüber lernen und bewegen

  • WORKING STUDENT: Du befindest dich aktuell in einem Studium und bringst idealerweise erste praktische Erfahrungen mit, zum Beispiel durch Praktika oder ehrenamtliches Engagement

  • AM TELEFON ZU HAUSE: Du hast schon mal jemanden am Telefon von etwas überzeugt — im Job, im Verein, im Nebenjob, egal.

  • AUF DEN PUNKT, OHNE KALT ZU WIRKEN: Du sagst in drei Sätzen, wofür andere zehn brauchen, und klingst dabei trotzdem wie ein Mensch. Handwerksbetriebe haben keine Zeit für Marketing-Sprache und merken sofort, wenn jemand welche spricht.

  • ZUVERLÄSSIG, NICHT VERHANDELBAR: Zugesagter Rückruf am Donnerstag heißt Donnerstag. Das ist bei uns Grundvoraussetzung, keine Stärke.

  • DU BRINGST WAS ZURÜCK: Nach fünfzig Gesprächen hast du eine Meinung dazu, was funktioniert. Du sagst sie, ohne dass wir danach fragen müssen.

  • DEUTSCH AUF MUTTERSPRACHNIVEAU: Unsere Partner sind deutsche Handwerksbetriebe. Das Gespräch läuft auf Deutsch, inklusive Zwischentöne und Dialekt am anderen Ende.

  • MINDESTENS 6 MONATE ZEIT: Kürzer lohnt sich für keinen von uns beiden. Bis du richtig gut in diesen Gesprächen bist, vergehen Wochen.


Unser Angebot

Wachstum & Kultur

Werde Teil eines Teams, das nicht nur fachlich durchstartet, sondern aktiv eine gesunde und nachhaltige Unternehmenskultur lebt. Bei uns zählt das Miteinander genauso viel wie der Erfolg.

Impact & Awareness

Deine Stimme hat Gewicht, im Büro und darüber hinaus. Neben deinem regulären Urlaub bekommst du zusätzliche freie Tage für Klimaaktivismus, Demos oder Projekte, die dir am Herzen liegen.

Flexibilität & Vertrauen

Gestalte deinen Arbeitsalltag nach deinem Rhythmus. Nutze unsere Flexdays, um mobil zu arbeiten – egal ob von zu Hause oder unterwegs innerhalb Deutschlands, immer in Absprache mit deinem Team.

Extra Benefits für dich

Wir machen deinen Alltag einfacher: Du bekommst einen flexiblen Bonus, den du nach Lust und Laune für Dinge einsetzen kannst, die dir Freude machen – ob Fitness, Kultur oder kleine Extras.

Verpflegung & Wohlbefinden

Wenn der Arbeitstag mal länger wird, sorgen wir dafür, dass niemand hungrig bleibt. Bestell dir über Wolt eine Mahlzeit direkt ins Büro – easy und lecker.

Community & Spirit

Wir verändern die Welt – und verlieren dabei nie den Spaß. Freu dich auf regelmäßige Offsites, Teamabende und unser legendäres „Bees & Beers“ als perfekten Ausgleich zu unserer Mission.

data.description:
Was du bei uns machen wirst:

TL;DR

Zasta ist die führende Steuer-App in den deutschen App Stores (schau selbst auf deinem Handy in der Kategorie Finanzen nach). 

Wir bauen kein Unternehmen über Headcount auf. Unsere Teams bestehen aus erfahrenen Expert:innen mit hoher Eigenverantwortung, kurzen Entscheidungswegen und einem klaren Anspruch an Qualität und Geschwindigkeit.

Wir suchen einen Chief of Staff mit außergewöhnlich hohem Drive und analytischer Stärke, der direkt mit unserem CEO an den wichtigsten strategischen Themen von Zasta arbeitet.

  • End-to-End Ownership: Von Analyse und Business Case über Partnerverhandlung und Scoping bis zu Go-live und messbarem Ergebnis.

  • Top-Profil: Sehr starker akademischer Track Record und typischerweise 3–8 Jahre relevante Erfahrung – z. B. Strategy Consulting + Operator-Rolle, Founders' Office oder General Management.

  • Business-relevante Projekte: Neue Geschäftsmodelle, Partnerschaften, Marketing Channels, regulatorische Themen, Markterweiterungen und andere strategische Initiativen.

  • Deutsch auf nahezu muttersprachlichem Niveau ist aufgrund unseres regulierten Steuerumfelds zwingend erforderlich.

  • Starkes Gehalt + VSOP, ein klarer Entwicklungspfad in eine operative Leadership-Rolle bei Zasta (wenn dein Weg dich stattdessen zur eigenen Gründung führt, unterstützen wir dich gerne mit einem Angel-Ticket).

Du bist für relevante strategische Themen von der ersten Idee bis zum messbaren Business Impact verantwortlich.

Achtung: Das ist keine klassische Stabs-, PMO- oder Koordinationsrolle.

Du arbeitest dich schnell in neue Themen ein, schaffst Struktur, entwickelst Business Cases, identifizierst und verhandelst mit Partner:innen und treibst die Umsetzung gemeinsam mit Product, Tech, Marketing und Operations bis zum Go-live.

Wir suchen jemanden, der Dinge baut und ins Ziel bringt, anstatt nur Entscheidungsvorlagen zu erarbeiten.

Deine Verantwortung

Du arbeitest direkt mit unserem CEO und eng mit dem Management Team an strategisch relevanten Initiativen. Deine Themen sind keine Side Projects. Sie bewegen relevante Line-Items in unserem Business Plan.

Je nach Projekt bedeutet das:

  • neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten identifizieren, auf Machbarkeit prüfen und umsetzen

  • komplexe, unstrukturierte Probleme in klare Hypothesen, Entscheidungen und Workstreams übersetzen

  • Business Cases und Economics entwickeln und kritisch challengen

  • externe Partner:innen identifizieren, bewerten und kommerzielle Konditionen verhandeln

  • gemeinsam mit Product, Tech, Marketing und Operations MVPs konzipieren und umsetzen

Wir messen dich nicht daran, wie gut deine Slides sind, sondern daran, ob du reale Probleme löst und messbaren Business Impact schaffst.

Zwei beispielhafte ProjekteEinen neuen Geschäftsbereich aufbauen

Rund um das „Altersvorsorgedepot“ entstehen in Deutschland neue Marktchancen.

Du bewertest, welche Rolle Zasta darin spielen sollte – von einer Affiliate-Partnerschaft bis zu einer tief integrierten Produktlösung.

Markt & Strategie → Business Case → Partner Sourcing → Verhandlung → MVP → Tech-Integration → Go-live

Du entwickelst die Economics, identifizierst geeignete Partner:innen, führst Verhandlungen, bewertest regulatorische und operative Anforderungen und bringst die gewählte Lösung gemeinsam mit Product und Tech in unser Produkt. Ein sauberes „Nein“ ist für uns genauso wertvoll wie ein Go-live – wenn die Economics oder Rahmenbedingungen nicht stimmen.

Einen neuen Marketingkanal erschließen

Wir wollen beispielsweise testen, ob sich Out-of-Home zu einem skalierbaren Performance-Marketing-Kanal für Zasta entwickeln kann (und ja: Wir meinen Performance, nicht nur Brand).

Du entwickelst Business Case und Testsetup, bewertest Anbieter und Inventar, verhandelst Konditionen und bringst die Kampagne gemeinsam mit Marketing und Brand live. Wenn Lukas Podolski Teil des Test-Setups sein soll, bekommen wir auch das hin. Anschließend entscheiden wir anhand klarer KPIs: Scale, iterate or stop.

Weitere Projekte können neue Partnerschaften, Pricing, regulatorische Themen, operative Skalierung, M&A, neue Produkte, Vertriebskanäle, vollständig neue Geschäftsmodelle oder interne Strukturen betreffen.


Was du idealerweise mitbringst:

Wir suchen eine außergewöhnlich starke Kombination aus analytischer Exzellenz, Geschwindigkeit und Ownership.

Du bringst mit:

  • einen sehr guten akademischen Track Record und einen sehr guten Abschluss von einer führenden Universität

  • typischerweise 3–8 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung

  • außergewöhnlich starke analytische und strukturierte Problemlösungsfähigkeiten

  • die Fähigkeit, dich sehr schnell und tief in neue und komplexe Themen einzuarbeiten

  • sehr gutes quantitatives und kommerzielles Urteilsvermögen

  • Sicherheit im Umgang mit Gründer:innen, Senior Stakeholdern, Führungskräften und externen Partner:innen

  • einen sehr hohen Anspruch an Qualität und Geschwindigkeit sowie einen starken Bias for Action

Wenn du ein Problem siehst, wartest du nicht auf Zuständigkeiten. Du übernimmst Ownership, schaffst Klarheit und bringst die Lösung ins Ziel.

Exzellentes Deutsch ist zwingend erforderlich

Du sprichst Deutsch auf nahezu muttersprachlichem Niveau und kannst komplexe Sachverhalte sprachlich präzise erfassen, formulieren und verhandeln.

Das ist für uns keine formale Anforderung: Zasta bewegt sich in einem stark regulierten Umfeld rund um Steuerberatung, Finanzprozesse und Verbraucherschutz. In vielen Fragestellungen kommt es auf juristische, steuerliche oder regulatorische Nuancen der deutschen Sprache an.

Du musst in der Lage sein, diese selbstständig zu verstehen, kritisch zu hinterfragen und präzise mit Steuerberater:innen, Partner:innen, Anwält:innen, Behörden und internen Teams zu kommunizieren.


Was wir dir bieten:

  • starkes Gehalt + VSOP

  • direkte Zusammenarbeit mit CEO und Management Team

  • außergewöhnlich viel Verantwortung und Entscheidungsspielraum

  • kurze Wege von einer guten Idee zur tatsächlichen Umsetzung

  • einen bewussten Entwicklungspfad in eine operative Leadership-Rolle bei Zasta

Wir suchen keinen Career Chief of Staff. Wir suchen einen zukünftigen Business Owner.

Im besten Fall übernimmst du nach dieser Rolle einen relevanten Teil des Unternehmens selbst – als Business Owner, VP oder in einer anderen Leadership-Funktion.

Und dein Weg muss nicht bei Zasta enden:

Wir würden uns freuen, wenn wir dich in einigen Jahren bei der Gründung deines eigenen Unternehmens mit einem Angel-Ticket unterstützen könnten.

data.description:
About REMATIQ

REMATIQ is changing how MedTech teams develop, document, and launch medical devices by building a highly specialised AI platform for regulated R&D, quality, and regulatory workflows.

We work with leading life sciences and MedTech companies to help them move faster while improving quality, traceability, and compliance. We are looking for an AI Deployment Strategist – MedTech Quality Management to help our customers transform complex quality and QMS workflows into practical AI-powered solutions.

We believe in the value of in-person collaboration and work in a hybrid setup, with the team coming together in our office in the heart of Berlin-Mitte typically four days per week.

What you’ll do

As an AI Deployment Strategist – MedTech Quality Management at REMATIQ, you will work closely with customers, Delivery, Product, and Engineering to drive customer projects, understand how MedTech quality teams work today, and help translate their workflows into high-impact AI use cases.

This is not an academic advisory role. You will be hands-on in customer projects, helping structure problems, drive workstreams, create materials, review outputs, and turn domain expertise into practical solutions.

You will:

  • Own and drive customer project workstreams from discovery through workflow design, implementation support, testing, iteration, and delivery.

  • Work directly with Quality, Operations, R&D, Regulatory, and cross-functional customer teams to understand their QMS processes and documentation, including SOPs and work instructions, CAPA and nonconformance handling, complaints and post-market surveillance, change control, supplier quality, audit readiness, and related product-development records, as well as the constraints, pain points, and opportunities for AI-powered improvement.

  • Bring deep MedTech quality management expertise across areas such as ISO 13485, FDA QMSR / 21 CFR Part 820, MDSAP, ISO 14971 risk management, design controls, CAPA, deviations, supplier quality, and internal and external audits — and act as a domain sparring partner for internal teams.

  • Create and review project deliverables such as customer workshop materials, process and workflow maps, QMS and standards gap analyses, impact assessments, target process designs, use-case specifications, and AI-generated outputs together with customer subject-matter experts.

  • Collect customer learnings and feedback and translate them into structured internal feedback for Product and Engineering.

  • Use AI tools actively to speed up your own work, create high-quality outputs faster, and improve how customer projects are delivered.

What we’re looking for

We are looking for someone who combines deep MedTech quality management expertise, strong project ownership, customer-facing communication, and a hands-on execution mindset.

You may be a strong fit if you have:

  • 5–8 years of relevant experience in MedTech quality management, QA/QM, QMS ownership, quality systems, quality operations, or a related consulting role.

  • Practical understanding of how a medical device QMS operates day to day, including areas such as document and change control, design controls, risk management, verification & validation, CAPA and nonconformance handling, complaints and post-market surveillance, supplier quality, training and competence, management review, and audits and inspections — and the ability to translate this expertise into AI-enabled use cases, project deliverables, and structured product feedback.

  • Strong project ownership: you can structure ambiguous work, align stakeholders, manage risks, define next steps, and drive cross-functional customer projects from problem understanding to delivery.

  • Strong customer-facing communication: you can build trust with Quality, Regulatory, Operations, R&D, and senior stakeholders, ask sharp questions, and explain complex topics clearly.

  • Hands-on execution mindset: you are comfortable creating materials, mapping workflows, reviewing outputs, synthesising findings, adapting to changing priorities, and driving work forward yourself.

  • Comfort with speed and change: REMATIQ is growing extremely fast, with the organisation doubling every 9–12 months. You are comfortable operating in a high-speed, high-agency environment with rapidly changing scope and responsibilities.

  • AI savviness: you actively use AI tools to improve your own work, move faster, create better deliverables, and explore new ways of working.

  • Fluency in English; German is a strong plus for German-speaking customer work.

Why join REMATIQ?

  • Rare timing: Join REMATIQ at a pivotal stage as we move from Seed toward Series A and prepare to significantly grow the team.

  • Real ownership: Own high-impact customer projects and see your work translate directly into outcomes for leading MedTech and life sciences companies.

  • Direct exposure: Work closely with founders, customers, product teams, and technical experts while building a network across the global MedTech and life sciences industry.

  • Purposeful work: Be part of a mission-driven team transforming how medical devices reach the market — in an industry where quality, compliance, and patient safety mean nothing can be left to chance.

  • Compensation & growth: Competitive salary plus equity, giving you a stake in the success you help create.

data.description:
Build the product engine behind the next generation of MedTech software.

REMATIQ is building AI software that helps life sciences and medical device companies bring products to market faster, without compromising the quality, traceability and compliance their industry demands.

We work with leading companies including Philips, Siemens Healthineers, B. Braun and Novartis, and have recently closed our Series A.

We believe in the value of in-person collaboration and work in a hybrid setup, with the team coming together in our office in the heart of Berlin-Mitte typically four days per week.

Now we’re looking for a hands-on Product Lead / Head of Product to help us turn ambitious product direction into exceptional shipped product.

The role

This is a player-coach role for someone who wants real product ownership without moving away from the product itself.

Our founder will continue to lead long-term product strategy, major capability bets and the frontier of where REMATIQ should go.

You will own how we get there.

You’ll take responsibility for the full product execution loop:

Customer insight → product ideas → prioritization → definition → engineering refinement → sprint execution → shipped product → learning.

You’ll lead a growing team of 2–3 Product Managers, raise the quality bar across the product organization, and still directly own one or two of our most important and complex product areas yourself.

You won’t be managing the process from the sidelines. You’ll be in the details with customers, PMs, engineers and designers, making decisions and helping the team ship.

What you’ll do

  • Own product execution end to end: Turn strategic direction and customer insight into clear priorities, well-defined product work and shipped outcomes.

  • Lead and develop the Product team: Manage 2–3 PMs, help them sharpen their judgment and execution, and establish a consistently high bar for product work.

  • Stay hands-on: Personally lead discovery, define product requirements, make prioritization decisions and own some of our hardest product areas.

  • Run product across multiple squads: Create clarity across Product, Engineering and Design and ensure teams move from idea to execution without unnecessary process or ambiguity.

  • Make the hard calls: Navigate competing customer needs, technical constraints and incomplete information, and make clear product decisions rather than simply facilitating consensus.

  • Build an AI-native product organization: Use AI deeply in your own work and help rethink how discovery, specification, prototyping, analysis and product development should work in an AI-first company.

  • Stay close to customers: Understand how sophisticated enterprise teams actually work, identify the problems worth solving and turn customer insight into scalable product rather than one-off features.

  • Continuously improve how we build: Identify where our product process needs more structure, where it needs less, and build the operating rhythm that helps REMATIQ ship better and faster as we scale.

What we’re looking for

You may be a strong fit if you:

  • Have led product for a B2B enterprise software product.

  • Have directly managed at least 2 Product Managers.

  • Are still deeply hands-on and comfortable running discovery, writing and refining product requirements, prioritizing trade-offs and working closely with Engineering.

  • Have owned product delivery across multiple squads or product areas.

  • Have strong product judgment and are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information.

  • Are genuinely AI-forward: you actively use AI in your work, understand how it changes product development, and have thoughtful views on what makes a product truly AI-native.

  • Communicate exceptionally well, both in writing and in conversation.

  • Operate with high ownership, pace and reliability.

We’ll be especially excited if you

This role can be office-based in Freiburg, Germany/ San Francisco, USA or remote-first, with a requirement to be in the office one full week per month.

About Black Forest Labs

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX—foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and video. We’re creating the generative models that power how people make images and video—tools used by millions of creators, developers, and businesses worldwide. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.

Why This Role

FLUX gets attention the moment people see it. Your job is to turn that attention into pipeline.

You'll own two motions where FLUX meets enterprises and partners in person: the events where customers experience the models firsthand, and the co-marketing engine with cloud and distribution partners who bring FLUX to the market. You’ll work directly with GTM, Partnerships, and our creative technologists. Our release cadence means there’s always a new reason to show up. Your job is to make sure we show up well and that every appearance has a number attached to it in order to effectively measure impact.

What you’ll work on

Events

  • Shape BFL's event calendar end-to-end: tier the opportunities, decide where we show up, and run the full events lifecycle: booths, demos, speaker slots, exec briefings, side events, follow up and more

  • Design event experiences that demonstrate the models, not just talk about them; working with Creative Technologists and FDEs on interactive demos and installations

  • Build the pre/post event machine: target lists for Sales, meeting orchestration on-site, pipeline attribution afterward. Every event has a number attached to measure impact (MQL’s)

  • Run BFL-hosted formats: customer dinners, launch events, and executive roundtables in key markets, plus side events at major moments (GTC, research oriented, etc.)

Co-marketing with partners

  • Own the co-marketing motion with our distribution and cloud partners; joint announcements, launch-day amplification, case studies, shared event presence

  • Coordinate partner marketing calendars around BFL launches so every major release lands with multiplied reach

  • Build repeatable co-marketing playbooks per partner tier, and negotiate marketing commitments into partnership conversations alongside the Partnerships team

GTM Enablement

  • Pitch decks

  • Solution marketing

Connecting the motions

  • Co-own the activation calendar with our social marketing team so events, partner moments, and social land together

  • Feed what you learn on the floor (what lands, the questions enterprises actually ask back into GTM and product marketing)

What We're Looking For

  • 3–6 years in field/event marketing, partner marketing, or integrated campaigns at a B2B tech company

  • You've run events end-to-end (from a 10-person exec dinner to a major conference presence) and can show the pipeline they produced

  • You've done co-marketing with large partners

  • You understand enterprise marketing: how buying committees work, what an exec briefing needs to accomplish, why attribution matters

  • 80%+ execution. You can build the run-of-show, brief the booth staff, etc.

  • Strong visual taste: our outputs are judged visually, and so are our activations

  • Comfortable with ambiguity, tight timelines, and launch weeks where everything happens at once

While not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:

  • Experience marketing generative AI, creative tooling, or developer-facing infrastructure

  • Existing relationships in the creative AI community

  • Experience working with cloud or platform partners on joint GTM

  • You've built an event or campaign that people in the industry still reference

  • Time spent working in the US, or in a role with significant US market ownership

How We Work Together

We’re a distributed team with real offices that people actually use. Depending on your location, you’ll either join us in Freiburg or SF at least 2 days a week (or one full week every other week), or work remotely with a monthly in-person week to stay connected. We’ll cover reasonable travel costs to make this possible. We think in-person time matters, and we’ve structured things to make it accessible to all. We’ll discuss what this will look like for the role during our interview process.

Everything we do is grounded in four values:

  • Obsessed. We are a frontier research lab. The science has to be right, the understanding deep, the product beautiful.

  • Low Ego. The work speaks. The best idea wins, no matter who said it. Credit is shared. Nobody is above any task.

  • Bold. We take the ambitious bet. We ship, we do not wait for conditions to be perfect.

  • Kind. People over politics. We treat each other with genuine warmth. Agency without empathy creates chaos.

If this sounds like work you’d enjoy, we’d love to hear from you.

data.description:
Die Chance

Im Mittelstand wird das Rechnungswesen in Teile zerlegt und weitergegeben. Einer bucht, einer baut den Abschluss, einer spricht mit dem Unternehmer. Am Ende kennt niemand das Unternehmen ganz, und der Inhaber bekommt Zahlen, mit denen er nicht steuern kann.

Vogel erwirbt eigenständige Beratungsunternehmen und baut sie zur stärksten Adresse ihrer Region aus. Mehrere Tausend mittelständische Unternehmen vertrauen uns ihre steuerlichen, kaufmännischen und strategischen Themen an. Für diese Unternehmen übernehmen wir das Rechnungswesen vollständig: die laufende Verarbeitung mit hohem Automatisierungsgrad, die handelsrechtliche Bilanzierung und darauf aufbauend Auswertung, Planung und Controlling.

Du führst deine Mandate vollständig durch die Zahlen, vom laufenden Rechnungswesen über den Abschluss bis in das Gespräch, in dem der Unternehmer seine Entscheidungen trifft. Es gibt keine Schnittstelle, an der du übergibst. Du führst ein Team und berichtest an die Geschäftsführung.

Was du verantwortest

Rechnungswesen und Bilanzierung

  • Verantworte das laufende Rechnungswesen deiner Mandate unter hohem Automatisierungsgrad und steigere diesen Grad weiter, statt Handarbeit zu verwalten. Dein Maßstab ist nicht, dass die Zahlen am Ende stimmen, sondern wie wenig manueller Aufwand dafür nötig war.

  • Verantworte den handelsrechtlichen Jahresabschluss samt Anhang und Bericht als eigenständiges Ergebnis für den Unternehmer, nicht als Vorstufe der Steuererklärung.

  • Definier, wann ein Abschluss abschlussfähig ist, und mach daraus einen Standard, der auch unter Fristendruck trägt, samt Vier-Augen-Regime in der Linie.

Steuerung und Beratung

  • Führ das Monats- oder Quartalsgespräch mit dem Unternehmer und übersetz die Zahlen in eine Handlungslinie. Dein Maßstab: Er kann danach entscheiden, nicht nur eine Zahl wiederholen.

  • Bau Planung und Steuerung auf dem laufenden Rechnungswesen auf: Ergebnis-, Bilanz- und Liquiditätsplanung mit Szenarien, Forecast, Soll-Ist-Abgleich, Deckungsbeitrag.

  • Begleite Finanzierungen und Bankgespräche, bereite ratingfähig auf und zeig die Liquiditätsreserven, die im Working Capital und im Forderungsmanagement liegen.

Team und Standard

  • Führ dein Team fachlich und disziplinarisch: Review, Eskalations-Entscheidungen, Leistungsgespräche, Mitwirkung im Einstellungsprozess.

  • Entwickle die Erfahrungsstufen in deiner Linie weiter. Wer welchen Abschluss baut und wer welches Steuerungsgespräch führt, ist eine Frage von Befähigung, nicht von Dienstalter.

  • Schneid die Steuerungsleistungen so zu, dass sie wiederkehrend tragen und mit dem Mandatsvolumen skalieren, statt bei jedem Mandat neu erfunden zu werden.

Fragen, auf die du die Antwort findest

  • Ein Mandant will die Steuerungsleistung nicht zahlen, weil sie der Steuerberater bisher mitgemacht hat. Wie grenzt du den Wert ab, und wo hältst du das Honorar?

  • Wann ist ein Abschluss abschlussfähig, und was tust du, wenn der Termin drückt und der Standard nicht erreicht ist?

  • Welche Auswertung braucht wirklich jeder Mandant, und welche nur der, der danach fragt?

Woran wir Erfolg messen

  • Nach 6 Monaten: Rund zehn handelsrechtliche Abschlüsse in eigener Verantwortung abgeschlossen und dabei den Standard gesetzt. Das Vier-Augen-Regime läuft, die ersten Steuerungsgespräche hast du selbst geführt, und du kennst dein Team persönlich.

  • Nach 12 Monaten: Mindestens fünf Mandate im laufenden Rechnungswesen um rund zwanzig Prozent effizienter, messbar an Durchlaufzeit und Handarbeitsanteil. Mindestens ein Steuerungsthema über die Finanzbuchführung hinaus läuft bei mehreren Mandaten.

  • Nach 24 Monaten: Ein Qualitätsniveau, das über den Bestand messbar ist und nicht an einzelnen Personen hängt. Die Beratungsleistung auf dem Rechnungswesen trägt als wiederkehrende Umsatzlinie, und dein Team ist über die erste Ebene hinaus gewachsen.

  • Wohin es führt: in die Verantwortung für Accounting und Controlling über mehrere Standorte. Das ist die Management-Karriere, entschieden an einer Linie, die den Standard eigenständig trägt, und nicht am Berufsjahr.

Was du mitbringst

  • Du hast das Wirtschaftsprüfer-Examen bestanden oder stehst kurz davor, oder du trägst seit mehreren Jahren die Verantwortung für handelsrechtliche Abschlüsse mittelständischer Gesellschaften.

  • Du hast Abschlüsse nicht nur geprüft, sondern erstellt, und kennst den Unterschied zwischen einem Abschluss, der formal steht, und einem, der eine Aussage trifft.

  • Du hast wirtschaftlichen Sachverstand schon direkt zum Unternehmer getragen und nicht nur an eine Führungskraft berichtet.

  • Du beherrschst die HGB-Bilanzierung im Mittelstand mit ihren echten Streitpunkten, von der Bestandsbewertung über unfertige Leistungen bis zu Gesellschafterkonten, und kannst deine Position vertreten.

  • Du arbeitest mit KI als selbstverständlichem Werkzeug für Plausibilisierung, Anomalie-Erkennung in Kontenbewegungen, Planungslogiken und Drafting.

  • Du hältst den Qualitätsstandard, auch wenn der Termin drückt, bringst die Demut mit, von Praktikern zu lernen, und setzt in allem den höchsten Standard, weil Mittelmaß für dich keine Option ist.

Ein Plus, keine Bedingung

  • Die Mechanik von Planung und Finanzierung: integrierte Mehrjahresplanung, Investitionsrechnung, Rating-Logik gegenüber Banken.

  • Genug steuerliches Gespür, um zu erkennen, wann eine handelsrechtliche Entscheidung steuerlich relevant wird. Die Lösung musst du nicht selbst kennen.

  • Kein kanonischer Lebenslauf nötig: Bilanzbuchhalter mit langjähriger eigener Abschlussverantwortung, der faktisch schon das Steuerungsgespräch geführt hat; Steuerberater mit Rechnungswesen- und Controlling-Schwerpunkt; Prüfer aus dem Verbundbereich mit Mittelstands-Tiefe. Wir bewerten am Beitrag, nicht am Etikett; die ausgewiesene Spanne bezieht sich auf das Primärprofil, und ein anderer Hintergrund startet zu einem anderen Marktpreis und konvergiert nach zwölf Monaten bewährter Leistung auf das Rollen-Niveau.

Was diese Rolle ist, und was nicht

  • Dieselben Unternehmen über Jahre, kein Prüfungszyklus. Du siehst, was aus deiner Arbeit wird, statt einmal im Jahr zu testieren und wieder zu gehen.

  • Bilanz und Gespräch, kein reines Controlling. Du trägst den Abschluss selbst. Wer die Zahlen nur interpretieren will, ist hier falsch.

  • Gestalten, kein fertiges Regelwerk. Wie der Standard aussieht, wie weit die Automatisierung geht und welche Steuerungsleistungen wir anbieten, entscheidest du mit.

Warum Vogel

  • Ein Mandat, eine Hand. Kein Übergeben, keine Schnittstelle. Dein Abschluss ist die Grundlage deines eigenen Beratungsgesprächs, und das gibt es im Markt selten.

  • Die Fleißarbeit nimmt dir das System ab. Erfassung und Abstimmung laufen weitgehend maschinell, und unser eigener Jahresabschluss mit KI ist der Beleg. Was bleibt, ist Beurteilung und das Gespräch.

  • Du willst entscheiden: Abschluss-Standard, Vier-Augen-Regime und Aufstellung deines Teams. Vogel ist hierarchisch in der Entscheidung, flach in der Kommunikation, autonom in der Ausführung. Leistung wird gefeiert, nicht versteckt, ohne Konsens-Theater.

  • Substanz im Rücken. Ein profitables, wachsendes Unternehmen mit etablierten Mandanten. Der Bestand ist da, du musst ihn nicht erst gewinnen.

FAQ

1. Was ist Vogel – und wo arbeitet ihr?

Vogel ist eine der führenden Mittelstandsberatungen Deutschlands – seit 1959, inhabergeführt in zweiter Generation, mit eigenem Kapital – und baut daraus die führende Beratungsplattform für den Mittelstand. Wir arbeiten an drei Standorten: Aalen als gewachsenem Stammsitz, Bopfingen im Kerngeschäft und München als neuem Hub. An allen dreien suchen wir quer durch die Funktionen – von Steuerberatung über Beratung bis zu den Teams, die das Fundament darunter bauen.

2. Wie sind die Gehaltsbänder zu verstehen?

Bewusst breit – und an jeder Stelle ausgewiesen, bevor du dich bewirbst. Wir differenzieren nach Track Record und Marktwert, nicht nach Abschluss: knappe, stark gefragte Profile am oberen Ende, weniger knappe am unteren. Die ausgewiesene Spanne ist kein Verhandlungsspielraum, sondern eine Profil-Skala – zwei Menschen mit ähnlicher Erfahrung können bei uns unterschiedlich verdienen. Was das obere Ende bestimmt, ist der Reifegrad, nicht die Zahl der Berufsjahre und nicht das Verhandlungsgeschick.

3. Wie viel – und wie – wird bei Vogel gearbeitet?

Gemessen wird an dem, was du bewegst, nicht an Stunden. Ehrlich ist aber auch: Wer 9-to-5 sucht, ist bei uns nicht die erste Adresse. Wir suchen Menschen, die aus eigenem Antrieb intensiv arbeiten, weil die Aufgaben es wert sind. Wie du deine Zeit verteilst, ist weitgehend deine Sache. Was wir teilen: Wir arbeiten präsent zusammen und sehen uns im Normalfall täglich im Büro – Kultur, Sparring und die besten Ideen entstehen in der täglichen Nähe. Wir sind keine Remote-Company und haben keine großen Home-Office-Policies; einzelne Remote-Tage sind kein Problem.

4. Wie läuft die Bewerbung?

Schlank, schnell, transparent – und nach Profil gestaffelt. In der Regel sind es vier Schritte: eine schriftliche Aufgabe, in der du zu acht Fragen Position beziehst – KI ist ausdrücklich erlaubt, wir bitten nur um eine kurze Selbstauskunft dazu; ein Gespräch von einer halben Stunde; eine gemeinsame Arbeitssitzung an einem echten Problem aus unserem Alltag; und ein Termin vor Ort mit dem Team und gemeinsamem Essen. Wie viele Schritte es tatsächlich werden, hängt von der Rolle ab: Bei Praktikum und Werkstudium fällt der Vor-Ort-Termin weg, für Schülerjobs genügt ein Gespräch, bei Senior-Rollen kommt ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsnachmittag dazu. Vorab kannst du einen Zehn-Minuten-Call buchen, in dem nur du fragst. In der Regel hörst du nach jedem Schritt innerhalb von 48 Stunden von uns.

5. Wie funktioniert die variable Vergütung?

Quartalsweise an Leistung gekoppelt, qualitativ bewertet. Die Skala steigt mit dem Level: bis 20 % Associate, 27,5 % Manager, 35 % Senior Manager, 42,5 % Director, 50 % VP. Erwartungswert bei guter Leistung – du erfüllst die Anforderungen, setzt eigene Akzente, bestehst den Keeper Test – liegt bei rund 50 % des Maximums; der Maximalbonus ist nicht der Normalfall. Im Fokus steht eine ganzheitliche Beurteilung durch deine Führungskraft anhand von sechs Kriterien: Impact, Judgement, Communication, Execution, Growth und Values.

6. Wie entwickle ich mich – welche Karrierewege gibt es?

Zwei aktive Wege: die IC-Karriere (fachliche Tiefe, Expertenlaufbahn) über die Stufen Expert, Senior, Lead und Principal – und die Management-Karriere (Führung, Personalverantwortung) über Manager, Senior Manager, Director und VP. Beide werden gleich vergütet, und beide müssen nicht nach oben führen: Wer auf einer Stufe bleibt und dort weiter in die Tiefe geht, ist bei uns genauso richtig. Die Richtung wählst du nach dem Onboarding, meist in Jahr 1–3. Berufseinstieg ist kein Sonderweg, sondern der frühe Teil derselben Strecke – vom Werkstudenten oder Praktikanten zum Associate, für die Besten ohne erneutes Bewerbungsverfahren.

7. Team, Kultur, Urlaub?

Das gemeinsame Mittagessen ist der tägliche Ankerpunkt – wer im Büro ist, isst mit; erwartet, nicht kontrolliert. Das Abendessen ist dasselbe Angebot ohne jede Erwartung. Beides ohne Eigenanteil. Dazu Social Events und Offsites in regelmäßigem Rhythmus – nicht als Pflichtprogramm, sondern weil ein gutes Team auch abseits der Arbeit Zeit teilt.

Benefits sind bei uns nicht das Sahnehäubchen, sondern das, was Intensität über Jahre tragbar macht: Examensförderung mit 25.000 EUR Qualifizierungsbudget und drei Monaten Freistellung, 100-prozentige Übernahme der Kinderbetreuung, EGYM Wellpass, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, Job-Ticket mit 90 % Zuschuss, Homeoffice-Ausstattung und ein Gerät deiner Wahl aus unserem Katalog, ein Buch im Monat aus dem Vogel-Kanon – und KI-Tools ohne Token-Limit und ohne Budgetdeckel. Urlaub: 28 Tage.

🏢 Who we are

A team from Germany with the vision to make advanced network security accessible for everyone

We are a software company developing an open source zero-trust network security platform that is both easy to use and affordable for teams of all sizes and budgets. Our mission is grounded in a simple yet powerful belief: secure private networking is a fundamental right of every modern company.

Since our launch on GitHub in 2021, we have gained trust among thousands of companies seeking secure and seamless solutions for connecting remote employees and infrastructure. By replacing traditional centralized VPNs, NetBird has become a trusted choice for modern network security, connecting today hundreds of thousands of users and machines worldwide. Our open source, community-driven approach has been a key driver of our success. We listen to our users, and their input helps us make network security better for everyone.

Want to see what we're working on? Check out our GitHub repo at https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird or https://netbird.io/knowledge-hub

✏️ What you will do

In Talent Acquisition at NetBird, you'll own how we find and win the people who build NetBird. We're growing fast, with lots of roles to fill across Engineering, GTM and Operations. Today our founders and hiring managers run most of the process themselves. You'll take that over end to end, from the first conversation to a signed offer, and build the hiring engine we need as we scale. You'll work closely with our Chief of Staff and every team lead.

You will:

  • Own full-cycle hiring across Engineering, GTM and Operations, from role kickoff to offer and close.

  • Source proactively for hard technical roles (Go, networking, platform, security), through GitHub, the open source community, events and your own network, instead of waiting for inbound.

  • Run the first conversation with candidates and be the person they trust throughout the process.

  • Partner with hiring managers to sharpen role definitions, scorecards and interview loops, and help interviewers give clear, consistent feedback.

  • Own job postings, interview plans, pipeline hygiene and reporting, so everyone knows where each role stands.

  • Track what matters, from time to hire and pipeline conversion to offer acceptance, and use it to fix what's slowing us down.

  • Turn our open source presence into an employer brand that makes great people want to talk to us.

  • Run offers and closing together with the founders, and hand new hires over smoothly to onboarding.

This is a hands-on role in a small team. You'll run searches yourself, and you'll shape how hiring works at NetBird as we grow.

🔎 What we are looking for

We're looking for a recruiter who can hold their own in a conversation with a senior engineer, likes structure, and gets energy from closing great candidates. Many of the best recruiters we know learned the craft at a recruiting agency or in a fast-growing startup, and if that's you, we'd especially love to hear from you. Agency experience counts as much as in-house: we care about how well you source, assess and close, not where you did it.

Must-Haves

  • 2 to 5 years of full-cycle recruiting experience with a strong share of technical roles, at a recruiting agency or in-house at a startup or scale-up.

  • A track record of sourcing and hiring software engineers, ideally for backend, infrastructure or security roles.

  • Enough technical curiosity to understand what our teams build and to tell a strong engineering profile from a keyword match.

  • You work with data and use it to improve the process, not just report on it.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English. You write outreach people actually answer.

  • You work AI native. You use AI tools every day, for example to source, screen or draft outreach, and you know where they help and where they don't.

  • Comfortable in a fast-growing team where processes are still being built.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience hiring for open source, developer tools, infrastructure or security companies.

  • Experience hiring GTM roles such as Sales, Solutions Engineering or DevRel.

  • Experience hiring across Europe, including relocation to Berlin.

  • Experience building an employer brand or a talent community from scratch.

🌟 What makes you a great fit

These are the values we work by as a team, and what they mean for this role:

  • Own the outcome: Small team, real scope. You own each role until the right person signs, and you fix the process instead of working around it.

  • Default to candor: Direct, kind, and specific, with candidates, hiring managers and founders alike. You say no early and explain why.

  • Stay close to the user: You take the time to understand our product and the community behind it, so you can explain to candidates why NetBird matters.

😌 What's in it for you

We know that happy and supported team members build the best products. That's why we offer:

  • Competitive compensation including salary and equity.

  • Hybrid Cowork model in our new Berlin office with flexibility for remote days.

  • Build the function and grow with it: You set up how NetBird hires, with real ownership from day one and room to grow into a lead role as the team scales.

  • Close collaboration with our founders and every team lead.

  • The essentials done well: team lunches, team events, and health and fitness programs (e.g., Wellpass).

If you don't tick every box, apply anyway.

The team:

The Comms team builds and manages the technology that enables Kraken to communicate with customers across multiple channels, including phone, email, live chat and physical post. The team is responsible for both the underlying systems and the product features that support these customer interactions.

A key area of the team is voice and telephony, where they build the technology used by energy and support specialists to speak with customers. This includes managing real-time calls, handling customers and specialists joining or leaving calls, responding to connection and network issues, and ensuring calls can be reliably maintained or recovered when problems occur.

Unlike more traditional transactional backend systems, much of the Comms technology is highly real-time and event-driven. The team works with event streams, queues and continuously changing system states to manage interactions as they happen.
The team also integrates with third-party communication providers, such as Twilio, which supports Kraken’s phone networks and email sending.
Overall, Comms sits at the intersection of engineering, product and customer operations, building the technology that enables Kraken’s customer-facing teams to communicate effectively and reliably with customers.

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role:

As Training Coordinator, you'll support Abound's learning and development by planning, running and monitoring training across our operational teams. You'll work closely with the QA and Training Manager, operations and site managers, subject matter experts and external trainers. Together, you'll make sure training meets business goals and our regulatory obligations under the FCA's Consumer Duty, CONC, MCOB and SM&CR.

You'll keep things running day to day. That means scheduling sessions, keeping records accurate and audit-ready, and making sure every new starter moves smoothly from day one to full competence. Additionally you will support the teams in supporting colleagues who may required additional training and support to regain competency status.

What you'll be doing:

Planning and scheduling

  • Create and manage training schedules across Customer Service, Collections, Credit Operations and new business lines.

  • Organise classroom and virtual training sessions: book rooms, trainers, systems access and equipment, and send joining instructions.

  • Coordinate new starter induction, including shadowing and buddy pairings (the "I do, we do, you do" model) and sign-off milestones, including role play based tasks.

Training materials and resources

  • Develop or coordinate training materials, e-learning and job aids, working with subject matter experts.

  • Keep training content and Confluence operating procedures current, version-controlled and in step with policy and regulatory change.

Records, reporting and compliance

  • Track attendance and maintain accurate, audit-ready training and competency records for every colleague.

  • Make sure statutory and regulatory training is completed on time. This includes Consumer Duty, vulnerable customers, financial crime and AML, data protection (UK GDPR), complaints handling (DISP) and the SM&CR Conduct Rules.

  • Prepare regular management information on training completion, competency status and outcomes for the QA and Training Manager and senior leaders.

Needs analysis and evaluation

  • Assess training needs through consultation with managers, QA results, complaints data, performance data and job analysis.

  • Turn QA findings into targeted refresher training and coaching sessions.

  • Evaluate how effective training is (feedback, assessments, QA scores before and after) and recommend improvements.

Suppliers and budget

  • Liaise with external trainers and providers, raise purchase orders, manage invoices and track spend against the training budget.

Who you are:

  • Experience coordinating training, L&D or onboarding, ideally in a contact centre or financial services setting.

  • Strong communication and organisational skills, with confidence working with managers at all levels.

  • Able to juggle several priorities, with excellent attention to detail and accurate record-keeping.

  • Understanding of adult learning principles and e-learning techniques.

  • Confident with Microsoft Office, PowerPoint and spreadsheets for tracking and reporting.

Ideally you'll also have:

  • Experience in an FCA-regulated firm, and awareness of Consumer Duty, CONC, MCOB, SM&CR or T&C regimes.

  • Knowledge of instructional design and learning management systems (LMS).

  • Experience with Confluence or similar knowledge-management tools.

A training or L&D qualification (for example CIPD Level 3, or a Level 3 Award in Education and Training).

What we offer:

  • Everyone owns a piece of the company - equity

  • Hybrid with 3 days a week in the office

  • 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays

  • 2 paid volunteering days per year

  • One month paid sabbatical after 4 years

  • Employee loan

  • Free gym membership

  • Team wellness budget to be active together - set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering

data.description:
🌍 About Outpost

Global expansion is broken. Without a local entity, conversion rates fall, costs rise, and compliance gets messy. Outpost fixes it.

Outpost is your modular back office for global commerce. Pick only what you need - tax, payments, treasury, or operations - and unlock new markets without the overhead. Sometimes we act as Merchant of Record, taking on tax and compliance risk. Other times, we give you the tools to do it yourself.

Sell anything, anywhere. Without compromise.

🧠 The Role

We're hiring a second Executive Assistant to support our CEO.

We already have an EA, and she isn't going anywhere. You'll report to the CEO and work alongside her: she keeps inbound, customer routing and the investor-facing side, takes diary, travel, logistics, internal admin, and hiring coordination. You'll join to take a defined set of workstreams off that plate.

Roughly 70% of this role is executive support. The other 30% is hiring - and that's where the leverage is. We run a five-stage interview loop across engineering, ops, product, GTM and tax, hiring around two people a month. Someone needs to own the machinery: scheduling across five calendars and four countries, keeping candidates warm, chasing feedback, making sure nobody good goes cold because a diary didn't line up.

This is a role for someone early in their career who is unusually organised and wants to learn how a company actually gets built. You won't be handed a finished process. You'll be shown how we do things today, and expected to make it better.

🧩 What You'll Do

Own the CEO's diary and logistics

  • Run scheduling day to day - booking, moving, protecting focus time, resolving clashes before they become problems

  • Book and manage international travel, and rebuild it when a flight moves

  • Prepare meeting packs: who's in the room, what they want, what happened last time

  • Track and chase the follow-ups nobody wrote down

Do the work he never sees

  • The highest-value work here is invisible. He shouldn't know it happened - he should just find the day went smoothly

  • Fix problems before they reach him: the double-booking, the missing dial-in, the visa that needed renewing

  • Do the quiet prep - background on a person he's meeting, what was agreed last time, the numbers checked before a deck goes out

  • Anticipate. If a trip is booked, the transfer, the dinner and the buffer around the flight are already handled

  • The fewer questions he has to ask you, the better you're doing the job

Own hiring coordination

  • Run scheduling across the full interview loop - five stages, multiple interviewers, several time zones

  • Keep the pipeline clean: trackers, interview feedback, stage-by-stage conversion

  • Build target lists for open roles and help manage outreach

  • Be the candidate's point of contact - fast, warm, human. How we treat candidates is how we're judged

  • Coordinate offers, references, contracts, start dates, and new-hire onboarding logistics

Keep the company running

  • Support board and investor prep alongside the CEO, Chief of Staff and our senior EA

  • Help run internal comms: all-hands, offsites, company updates

  • Manage supplier, tooling and expense admin so nobody else has to think about it

  • Spot the recurring problem and fix it permanently rather than solving it again next week

💥 Example Projects

  • Rebuild a full week of CEO travel in an afternoon after a fundraising meeting moves

  • Take time-to-offer from three weeks to ten days by fixing scheduling and feedback bottlenecks

  • Build the candidate tracker that shows conversion at every interview stage, and run it weekly

  • Own the logistics for a board meeting: pre-reads, agenda, materials, follow-ups

  • Organise a company offsite for a team split across London, Amsterdam and beyond

  • Write down how you do your job so the next person can pick it up in a week

🧱 What We're Looking For

Ideal background:

  • 1–3 years in an EA, team assistant, recruiting coordinator or ops support role - ideally at a startup or fast-growing tech / fintech company

  • Any recruiting coordination exposure is a plus, but we'll teach it if you're quick

  • Comfortable in a company without much process, because you've worked in one before

  • Fluent with modern tooling (Notion, Slack, Linear, ATS, scheduling tools and AI) and quick to pick up new ones

  • Excellent written English. You'll write on the CEO's behalf

Signals we care about:

  • Ridiculous bias for action - you solve, not observe

  • Extremely organised, and visibly so. Nothing gets dropped, nothing needs chasing twice

  • Strong EQ - you know how to read a room, a candidate, or a blocker

  • Sound judgement - you know what to decide yourself and what to escalate, and you sit on neither

  • Discreet. You'll see comp, term sheets and candidate conversations before most of the team

  • Curious and resourceful - you can figure anything out

  • You improve what you touch. The second time you do something, it should be faster than the first

What this role is not:

  • Not a diary-only role - you'll own hiring, onboarding and internal operations too

  • Not a pure recruiter role - hiring is a third of the job, not the whole of it

  • Not a role for someone who needs defined processes and hierarchy to be effective

  • Not a stepping stone you can coast through. The exposure is real, and so is the pace

🚀 Why This Role Is Different

Most assistant roles are about keeping someone else's life tidy. This one is about making a company move faster.

You'll own hiring coordination, which at our stage is one of the highest-leverage things we do — the people you help bring in will shape what Outpost becomes. And you'll get a front-row view of a Series A fintech being built, with two people above you invested in teaching you how it works.

We expect whoever is in this role to grow rapidly, and we'll back you every step of the way.

🦾 Outpost Team

Our team were leaders at Revolut, Airwallex, Adyen, Sumup and Wayflyer - and we're backed by top-tier investors who have built or backed some of the world's leading fintechs.

🧾 What We Offer

  • Equity and salary in a well-funded startup

  • Ability to own your work and move fast

  • World-class training from operators who've scaled globally

  • A global mission with real impact

  • Low politics, high output

  • Chance to grow into a senior role fast

  • A culture of builders, not talkers

🌎 Reach Out

Learn more

  1. Outpost Culture

  2. Outpost founder

About Ema

Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs.

We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale.

Role: Senior Support Specialist (Enterprise Agentic AI)

Company: Ema Unlimited Inc.
Location: London
Employment Type: Full-time/Remote

 
 

1. About Ema (Why Ema)

Ema is building the world’s first Universal AI Employee — a production-grade agentic AI platform that automates real enterprise workflows across HR, IT, Finance, and Operations.

Ema’s customers do not run demos. They replace mission-critical, manual business processes with agentic AI systems that operate across multiple SaaS tools, APIs, and human-in-the-loop workflows.

In this world, support is not reactive. Support is production reliability, trust preservation, and system learning. At Ema, Senior Technical Support Specialists are operators of live AI systems, not ticket handlers.

 

2. Role Overview

The Senior Support Engineer owns the health, reliability, and trustworthiness of Ema’s deployed agentic AI systems in production. This role sits at the intersection of:

  • AI behavior

  • Workflow orchestration

  • Enterprise integrations

  • Customer trust

  • Engineering feedback loops

This is: ❌ Not L1 / call-center support, ❌ Not a “just escalate to engineering” role, ❌ Not reactive firefighting only

This is: A senior technical escalation role, A production debugging and RCA role, A partner to Engineering, Product, and Implementation, A role with real authority during incidents

3. Impact of the Role

Impact at Ema

  • You are the last line of defense between a production issue and customer trust erosion

  • You prevent small failures from turning into account-level crises

  • You ensure learnings from incidents improve the product and delivery systemically

Impact on Customers

  • Customers trust Ema because issues are handled competently and transparently

  • AI failures are explained, mitigated, and prevented — not hand-waved

  • Production stability improves over time, not degrades

Impact on Your Career

  • You gain rare experience operating agentic AI systems in production

  • You build deep expertise across AI, integrations, and workflows

  • You can grow into Reliability Engineering, Implementation Leadership, or Product-facing roles

4. Core Problems You Will Solve

  • Diagnosing failures in multi-agent AI workflows

  • Deeply understanding Ema’s platform and providing workarounds/alternate approaches to customers facing issues

  • Debugging issues spanning:

    • AI behavior (false positives / negatives)

    • Workflow logic

    • Integrations (HRIS, ITSM, IAM, Finance)

    • Data quality

    • Platform configuration

  • Handling Sev-1 / Sev-2 customer specific incidents calmly under customer pressure

  • Help Engineering & Product teams Prevent repeated incidents through disciplined RCA

  • Converting noisy customer complaints into high-signal engineering feedback

 

5. Jobs To Be Done

5.1 Production Issue Ownership

  • Own customer-reported issues from intake to resolution adhering strictly to SLAs

  • Take responsibility for diagnosis, coordination, and closure; Importantly, provide workarounds to customers to unblock them while engineering fix is made

  • Ensure no issue is “lost” between teams

  • Act as technical owner even when multiple teams are involved

 

5.2 Debugging, Diagnosis & Sev 1/2 Issue Resolution

  • Debug agentic workflows end-to-end

  • Trace failures across agents, tools, integrations, and humans-in-the-loop

  • Identify whether issues are caused by:

    • Model behavior

    • Prompt / policy logic

    • Workflow orchestration

    • Integration constraints

    • Customer configuration

  • Provide clear, actionable root cause summaries

  • Resolve Sev 1 / Sev 2 Client issues; Escalate to the right team to help solve and close the issue. Keep customer communication calm, factual, and confidence-building

 

5.4 Customer Communication & Trust

  • Communicate during incidents without speculation or panic

  • Explain AI failures in a way customers can understand

  • Set realistic recovery timelines

  • Rebuild trust post-incident through transparency and follow-through

5.6 Feedback Loops to Engineering & Product

  • Write high-signal bug reports and incident summaries

  • Advocate for fixes based on customer impact, not noise

  • Help Product understand real production behavior

  • Ensure support insights influence roadmap and quality improvement

 

5.7 Support Operations & Excellence

  • Improve runbooks, playbooks, and diagnostics

  • Improve on-call hygiene and escalation clarity

  • Mentor junior support engineers

  • Raise the overall support bar at Ema

 

6. Traits We’re Looking For

Technical & Diagnostic Strength

  • Excellent debugging instincts

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguous systems

  • Able to isolate root cause across layers

Ownership & Reliability Mindset

  • Issues do not bounce — they get owned

  • Calm during incidents

  • Bias toward permanent fixes

Judgment & Communication

  • Knows when to escalate and when not to

  • Can say “we don’t know yet” credibly

  • Communicates clearly with both engineers and customers

Cultural Fit

  • Low ego, high accountability

  • Truth-seeking over blame

  • Respects both customer urgency and engineering quality

 
 

7. Required Qualifications

  • 6–9+ years in senior technical support, reliability, or production engineering roles

  • Experience supporting enterprise SaaS platforms in production

  • Strong understanding of:

    • APIs and integrations

    • Distributed systems

    • Logs, traces, and diagnostics

  • Experience handling escalations and incidents

  • Customer-facing experience with senior stakeholders

8. Preferred Background

  • Support or reliability roles in AI / automation platforms

  • Experience with workflow orchestration or agentic systems

  • Familiarity with AWS / GCP / Azure

  • Background in high-availability, 24×7 systems

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.

Ema Unlimited is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or genetics.

Metaview is an AI company focused on recruiting. We build AI agents that help world-class companies hire with radically more speed and precision. We automate the toil, and augment the human for companies like Brex, Affirm, Deel, ElevenLabs, and Airtable.

Founded by Siadhal and Shahriar after their experiences scaling Uber and Palantir, we’ve raised $110m from top-tier investors including Google Ventures and Insight Partners.

It's still day 0: Now is the time to re-engineer how work gets done with AI at the core, and our toughest challenges still lie ahead. We're looking for people seeking the hardest, most fulfilling work of their lives.

How we work

Four principles guide us:

  • Velocity. Optimize for rate of learning. Take action, get feedback, get better.

  • Hospitality. Sweat the experience. Delight customers, candidates and colleagues, even when it’s inconvenient.

  • Transparency. Public unless private. Share context openly within the company so people and agents can take initiative.

  • End-to-end. Deliver outcomes, not tasks. Step beyond your job description and see the work through.

The role

We're building strategic finance from scratch, and you'd be our first hire in it. You'd be the finance partner to every function, Sales, Marketing, Engagement and Product, helping decide how we price, where we invest and how we scale. You'd also own the numbers the company runs on: the operating model, the plan, and board and investor reporting. This is a hands-on role reporting directly to the Head of Finance, with no team between you and the work, and no part of it you won't touch. And you'll work closely on fundraising and investor relations.

We're looking for someone a few years into banking, consulting, PE or strategic finance who wants to own outcomes instead of advising on them. You'd build your own models, dashboards and workflows with AI at the core, not bolted on. And we want someone who'd rather build the process than inherit one.


Key ownership areas

  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Engagement and Product on the decisions that drive growth: pricing and packaging, sales capacity and quota planning, unit economics and payback, and GTM efficiency.

  • Own the operating model, annual plan and forecasts, and track how we perform against them.

  • Own monthly board and investor reporting, from the numbers through to the narrative.

  • Build the analytics and dashboards leadership uses to run the business.

  • Support fundraising and investor relations: model, materials, data room and investor Q&A.

What you bring

  • 2–4 years in investment banking, consulting, private equity or strategic finance.

  • You can build an operating model from a blank sheet, not just update one.

  • You turn messy data into a clear point of view, and can explain it plainly to a founder or a board member.

  • You take a problem and own it. You'd rather deliver the answer than hand off the deck.

  • You find building the playbook appealing.

  • You're excited to use AI to do analysis faster and better, not just to use the tools you're handed.

  • Bonus: SQL or data tooling (e.g. Hex), or exposure to B2B SaaS metrics.



What's in it for you

  • An environment that fosters cohesion, collaboration, and performance with transparency at the heart of what we do and how we communicate.

  • Supreme rate-of-learning as we re-orient how the world works with AI.

  • High compensation, through cash and equity.

  • Unlimited AI - Unlimited access to ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, and any other AI tools you need to move faster.

  • Build your own toolkit - We'll provide the latest hardware, software, and equipment you need to do your best work.

  • Ramp card for success - a company card to invest in the things that help you succeed:

    • Lunches and coffees with interesting people

    • Community memberships

    • Event attendance

    • Professional development

    • Home office upgrades

    • Books and learning resources
